LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DEMONSTRATIVES AND QUANTIFIERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3: Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we use demonstratives and quantifiers?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text
2. use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication
3. appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DEMONSTRATIVES AND QUANTIFIERS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DEMONSTRATIVES AND QUANTIFIERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers to a partner. (skill: use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text.
3. Practise this skill: use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of demonstratives and quantifiers communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we use demonstratives and quantifiers?
2. When do we use demonstratives and quantifiers?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify demonstratives and quantifiers in a given text.
5. Be able to: use demonstratives in sentences for clarity of communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
